finalText:
Found it. `processOrder.js` was manually managing the connection lifecycle instead of using the safe `withConnection` wrapper. When an order failed validation, the promise rejected before hitting the `pool.release()` line, so the connection stayed acquired forever.

The code had a comment about needing to bypass the wrapper for an old retry loop that no longer exists — the fix was just cleaning that up and using `withConnection` like the rest of the codebase does.

All 4 tests pass now, including the one that specifically checks for connection leaks on failure.
